general_guidance: Rest, stay hydrated, and monitor temperature. Mild fever can often be managed with rest and fluids.
when_to_see_doctor: If fever exceeds 103°F (39.4°C), lasts more than 3 days, or is accompanied by severe headache, rash, or difficulty breathing

general_guidance: Stay hydrated, rest, warm fluids like tea or soup can soothe throat irritation
when_to_see_doctor: If cough persists beyond 2 weeks, produces blood, or is accompanied by high fever or chest pain

general_guidance: Drink ORS (oral rehydration solution) or clean water frequently to prevent dehydration, eat light food
when_to_see_doctor: If diarrhea lasts more than 2 days, contains blood, or is accompanied by high fever or severe dehydration signs (dizziness, very little urination)

general_guidance: Clean the wound with clean water, apply an antiseptic if available, cover with a clean cloth or bandage
when_to_see_doctor: If bleeding doesn't stop after 10 minutes of pressure, wound is deep, or shows signs of infection (redness, swelling, pus)

general_guidance: Regular checkups at the nearest PHC/Anganwadi center, balanced nutrition, iron and folic acid supplements as advised
when_to_see_doctor: Any bleeding, severe abdominal pain, reduced fetal movement, or swelling in hands/face should be checked immediately at a health facility
